Site survey

Investigate your space.

Look outside with an adult. Do you have tall trees, open flying room, shrubs, or a quiet place for a nest box?

Habitat checklist
Your yard, from above

Draw a simple map in Freeform on your iPad, export it as an image, then upload it here.

What to look for

Follow the trees.

Nuthatches and chickadees often favor wooded places. Swallows need open sky. Flickers may search for ants on the lawn.

Hands-on workshop

Build sequence
Safety: An adult handles power tools, cutting, drilling, and ladder work. Use untreated wood, ventilation and drainage, and a clean-out opening as the chosen plan directs. Do not add an outside perch.
Working with wood

Measure twice.
Cut once.

A house that is safe matters more than a house that is fancy.

09
Bonus / cold weather

A winter roost box.

Nesting boxes help birds raise chicks. Roost boxes are different: they can offer a sheltered place to rest during cold weather.

Illustrated idea

Conceptual illustration only. The downloadable Audubon design has the actual cut sizes and assembly requirements.

What makes it different?
  • It is for resting and staying sheltered, not raising babies.
  • A typical roost box puts the entrance lower than many nest boxes to help retain warmer air.
  • The box needs a clean-out method and a safe mount.
  • Use the published plan instead of copying this illustration's proportions.
Open the roost box plan ↗
Seasonal question

What do the birds need when it gets cold?

Food, water, protective cover, and safe places to rest are valuable habitat features—whether or not birds use a roost box.
